title: headphones/headset/mic selector dialog on plug event
line: Plugging something into a headset combo jack now shows a notification asking whether it is headphones, a headset or a microphone, and switches the output and microphone to match.
explanation: On combo jacks the kernel only reports that something was plugged in, not whether it has a microphone. The sound server marks the headphones as available and the headset and jack microphones as 'unknown', all in one availability group, so only the output switched and the headset microphone stayed unused until picked by hand. Plasma never read that information. pulseaudio-qt now exposes each port's availability group, and plasma-pa's kded module watches card ports: when a jack's headphones become available while its microphones are 'unknown', it shows a notification with Headphones / Headset / Microphone buttons (like GNOME's dialog) that sets the matching output and input ports, makes them default, and moves the other direction off the jack (e.g. Microphone moves the output back to Speakers).

commits.message:
Port: add availabilityGroup

Ports behind the same jack share an availability group: the server uses
it to say that it can't tell whether headphones, a headset or a mic was
plugged in. Expose it so that clients can ask the user which one it was.

CCBUG: 424273

kded: ask what was plugged into a headset jack

Combo jacks can't tell headphones, headsets and mics apart, so only the
output switched and the headset microphone stayed unused. When one is
plugged in, a notification now asks which it was and sets both ports.

BUG: 424273
